name: Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Aviral Kumar, Vincent Zhuang, Rishabh Agarwal, Yi Su, John D. Co-Reyes, Avi Singh et al. (18 authors); lead affiliation Google DeepMind
venue: ICLR 2025 (Oral); first posted as arXiv preprint Sep 2024
reflection_type: verbal-self-critique (intrinsic self-correction: the model revises its own prior answer over a second turn using only a fixed self-correction instruction, with no external critic or tool feedback at inference). The corrective behavior itself is instilled via reinforcement learning.
feedback_source: Two distinct signals must be distinguished. At TRAINING time the improvement signal is an environment/verifiable reward (answer-correctness oracle: final-answer correctness for MATH, unit-test pass for code) computed over self-generated correction traces. At TEST/INFERENCE time there is NO external feedback or reward access; the model self-corrects intrinsically using only a self-generated/in-context self-correction prompt.
iteration_structure: iterative-refine over a small fixed number of turns (multi-turn, typically 2 attempts: first attempt then a self-correction revision; extended to 3 attempts in the rebuttal/Gemma experiments). Sequential self-correction, not tree/MCTS search.
reflection_object: output content / reasoning chain (the second-turn revision rewrites the answer and its solution reasoning) AND model weights (the self-correction capability is baked into the policy parameters via RL gradient updates). The reflective behavior is parametric/learned, not just an in-context scaffold.
requires_training: RL (multi-turn online policy gradient, REINFORCE-style / RLOO-class with per-turn instantaneous reward and KL penalty); explicitly NOT SFT (the paper shows SFT/STaR/Pair-SFT variants are insufficient). Two-stage RL training.
reward_or_critic_model: verifiable reward (oracle answer-correctness / unit-test pass at training time) plus reward shaping (a reward bonus that amplifies traces flipping incorrect->correct between attempts and penalizes correct->incorrect). No separate trained reward model, no separate critic LLM, no stronger teacher model.
distillation_target: model-weights (the self-correction strategy is distilled into the policy's own parameters; no external episodic memory or reusable-skill artifact is produced).
emergent_vs_engineered: RL-emergent under an engineered training recipe: the self-correction behavior is learned/instilled by the multi-turn RL objective (with Stage I initialization + Stage II reward bonus) rather than hand-prompted at inference like Reflexion. The two-stage design and reward shaping are engineered to prevent behavior collapse and distribution mismatch, but the resulting correction policy is acquired through RL, not a fixed scaffold.
memory_type: short-term/scratchpad (within a multi-turn episode the model conditions on its own first attempt and the self-correction instruction). No persistent long-term episodic memory or skill library.
memory_persistence: within-episode (the prior attempt is available as context only within the current multi-turn rollout; nothing is carried across separate test problems).
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a (no external memory store; the only persistence is the second-turn prefix within the episode and the learned weights).
error_localization_granularity: holistic/outcome-level / response-level: correction operates on the whole answer based on a scalar outcome correctness signal (final-answer correctness or unit-test pass); there is no step-level or token-level error attribution/localization.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task (refinement happens within a single problem's multi-turn episode, similar in spirit to Self-Refine but trained); transfer across tasks is via the learned weights generalizing to new problems, not via stored cross-task experience.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: mid-trajectory-recovery / post-hoc-revision within the same episode: the model produces a first attempt and then corrects it in a subsequent turn (intrinsic self-correction), rather than retrying on a fresh episode.
benchmarks: MATH (trained on MATH train split, evaluated on the uncontaminated MATH500 test set), HumanEval, MBPP-R (code repair), plus held-out generalization sets Functional MATH and MathOdyssey; additional Gemma 2 (2B) open-model experiments added in the rebuttal/appendix.
headline_result: With Gemini 1.0 Pro and Gemini 1.5 Flash, SCoRe achieves state-of-the-art intrinsic self-correction, improving the base models' self-correction by 15.6% on MATH and 9.1% on HumanEval. On MATH, SCoRe attains a +4.4% positive self-correction delta (Delta(t1,t2)) with Accuracy@t2 of ~23.0%; on code it raises MBPP-R from 47.3% to 60.6% and yields a 12.2% self-correction delta on HumanEval. It is described as the first method to obtain a positive intrinsic self-correction rate.
baselines: Base model with self-correction prompting (intrinsic prompting, prior 'Self-Correction is not effective' setting), STaR / REST-EM (filtered SFT on successful correction traces), Pair-SFT (synthetic incorrect->correct repair pairs), single-turn RL ('w/o multi-turn training'), and a single-turn RL on base-model-sampled first attempts variant. Reference points include GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4 gap on MBPP-R.
gains_vs_baseline: On MATH, SCoRe's +4.4% self-correction Delta(t1,t2) vs the strongest comparable SFT baseline Pair-SFT (~1.8% gain over base, and an effective +0.2% delta for single-turn RL on fixed base first-turns); SCoRe improves over base model self-correction by 15.6% (MATH) / 9.1% (HumanEval) and surpasses Pair-SFT by ~10.2% in self-correction gain on MATH. Crucially, prior SFT/prompting methods produce a NEGATIVE or near-zero self-correction delta, whereas SCoRe is net-positive.
compute_cost_profile: Training: multi-turn online RL with self-generated rollouts (two stages of policy-gradient training; no extra teacher/reward-model training). Inference: sequential self-correction adds turns; per the rebuttal each additional sequential turn costs ~2.5x less latency than the first attempt due to prefix caching, giving total latency ~1 + c*(T-1) (c<1) vs fully parallel sampling. Combined with self-consistency, parallel+sequential gives a 10.5% gain vs 7.4% for parallel-only at comparable budget.
known_limitations: Primary experiments on private Gemini 1.0 Pro / 1.5 Flash models (reproducibility limited; partially addressed with Gemma 2 2B in appendix). Restricted to math and code with verifiable correctness rewards (needs tasks with non-multiple-choice, checkable answers; lack of large public training splits for other domains like physics/chemistry). Trained for a small number of attempts (2, extended to 3); scalability to many turns and joint multi-turn training is open. Some design choices (large vs small KL, reward-shaping sign) are intricate; reviewers noted weak theoretical justification for the claimed generalization benefit of self-correction policies.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: intrinsic-only at inference (no oracle label, tool, or reward at test time), BUT requires a verifiable/oracle correctness reward during RL training (env-reward over self-generated traces). It removes the test-time oracle dependency that earlier 'effective' self-correction relied on, which is the paper's core claim of genuine intrinsic self-correction.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive: SCoRe achieves a positive intrinsic self-correction delta (e.g., +4.4% on MATH) without test-time label leakage, in contrast to prior methods (prompting, SFT/STaR, Pair-SFT) which are net-negative or near-zero. Efficacy is established on math/code with verifiable rewards.
calibration_effect: not-measured (the paper focuses on accuracy and self-correction deltas / fraction of incorrect->correct vs correct->incorrect flips; it does not report confidence-calibration metrics or a 'reasoning-tax' analysis).
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (SCoRe is a self-correction training method, not a failure-attribution/diagnosis tool; it does not classify failure modes or attribute responsible steps/agents). However, the paper diagnoses two failure modes of prior training approaches: distribution mismatch/shift and behavior collapse (minimal-edit non-correction).
failure_mode_addressed: Targets the 'superficial self-reflection' / non-correcting failure mode where models leave answers unchanged or make only minimal edits (behavior collapse), and the distribution-mismatch failure where offline SFT correction data does not match the model's own response distribution. It addresses error-loops/over-conservatism by reward shaping that rewards incorrect->correct flips and penalizes correct->incorrect changes.
builds_on: Findings that LLMs cannot reliably intrinsically self-correct (Huang et al. 2023, 'Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet'); STaR / Expert Iteration / REST-EM self-training (Zelikman et al.; Singh et al. 2023 'Beyond Human Data'); REINFORCE/RLOO-style policy gradient for LLMs (Ahmadian et al. 2024) and PPO/RLHF; process/outcome reward and MATH train/test protocol (Lightman et al. 2023 'Let's Verify Step by Step'); reflection/self-refinement scaffolds (Self-Refine, Reflexion) which it contrasts against; multi-turn RL framing.
extended_by_or_inspired: Inspired a wave of RL-based self-correction / self-improvement and self-distillation work in 2025-2026, including self-distilled RLVR and on-policy-distillation methods (e.g., 'Self-Distilled RLVR', 'Reinforcement Learning via Self-Distillation', 'Self-Distillation Zero: Self-Revision Turns Binary Rewards into Dense Supervision', 'Expanding the Capabilities of Reinforcement Learning via Text Feedback'), multi-turn self-correction and reasoning-model self-correction studies, and is widely cited as the reference training-based self-correction method alongside reasoning models (o1/R1-style) that exhibit emergent reflection.
reasoning_model_native: Not specifically: SCoRe trains general (non-reasoning-specialized) Gemini/Gemma models to self-correct via RL, predating and complementing o1/R1-style reasoning models. It is frequently discussed as a precursor/parallel approach to the emergent reflection seen in o1-style models, and reviewers noted its relevance to o1-like inference-time scaling, but it does not require a reasoning-model substrate.
on_policy_distillation_link: Strongly relevant: SCoRe is a canonical on-policy / self-generated-data RL method (training under the model's own distribution of correction traces with REINFORCE-style updates), and it is heavily cited by the 2025-2026 on-policy-distillation (OPD) and self-distilled-RLVR literature as a foundational self-correction-via-self-data approach, even though SCoRe itself is reward-driven RL rather than teacher-logit distillation.
sample_efficiency: Reported in turns/stages rather than trial counts: two RL stages (Stage I initialization to avoid collapse + Stage II reward-bonus amplification), each over self-generated multi-turn rollouts; effective with as few as 2 self-correction attempts (extended to 3). Exact rollout/gradient-step counts are not given in the public abstract/reviews.
